# Pre-registered PPM primary-source fixtures and noncompliance register

**Provenance:** [EBU Tech 3205-E, second edition November 1979](https://tech.ebu.ch/docs/tech/tech3205.pdf), §§ 2–3 and Table 2, with [ITU-R BS.645-2 (1992)](https://www.itu.int/dms_pubrec/itu-r/rec/bs/R-REC-BS.645-2-199203-I%21%21PDF-E.pdf) corroboration. These source-defined outputs were recorded in Kestrel's [PPM research handoff](../../memory/projects/kisuul/kestrelgaming/handoffs/2026-11-05-audio-ppm-metering-research-r01.md) **before this module's implementation**. They are not generated by the reference function.

| Isolated burst, ms | Carrier | Continuous indication | Required burst maximum | Allowed deviation |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 100 | 5 kHz | +8 dB | +8 dB | ±0.5 dB |
| 10 | 5 kHz | +8 dB | +6 dB | ±0.5 dB |
| 5 | 5 kHz | +8 dB | +4 dB | ±0.75 dB |
| 1.5 | 5 kHz | +8 dB | -1 dB | ±1 dB |
| 0.5 | ≥10 kHz, at least 5 cycles | +8 dB | -9 dB | ±2 dB |

Additional independently published EBU constraints: +9 dB continuous 5 kHz takes 10±2ms isolated burst to reach +7; +12→-12 dB falling return in 2.8±0.3s normal mode; 1kHz +9 must cross +8 within 150ms; overswing ≤0.5dB; variation within ±0.3dB from 31.5Hz to 16kHz; polarity reversal difference ≤0.5dB on specified asymmetric 1kHz; separate pulse tests and slow mode. **Not every historical test is implemented, and our model fails some.**

## What is trained and what is independent

**Trained/fitted:** The model's two exponential attack constants and weights were fitted using the above 0.5–100 ms burst expectations. Passing those same values across sample rates is a fit verification, **not an independent demonstration of standard conformance**. The source-documented expected outputs were independently published, but model parameters were selected using them.

**Independent numerical verification:** Optional SciPy lfilter implementation on seeded signals with an independent vectorized max-of-discounted-outputs identity; ordinary binary64 result comparison only, not physical or algorithm-family validation. Rate/phase holdouts and randomized callback partitions provide additional falsification opportunities but are not blinded external-instrument calibration.

**Explicit failed EBU criterion:** The model exhibits about **+2.15 dB at 31.5 Hz** and **-0.82 dB at 16 kHz** for a 400 ms unit-peak steady tone sampled at 48 kHz, compared to approximately +0.02 dB at 5 kHz. Section 2.3 requires ±0.3dB flatness from 31.5Hz to 16kHz. A unit test *requires this failure to be visible*, so a future repair must revise the known-failure ledger and introduce tests demonstrating actual compliance rather than silently removing a failing criterion.

**Known unavailable evidence:** IEC 60268-10 complete paywalled text, electrical I/O calibration, physical meter response, phase sensitivity across arbitrary carriers/programme, full impulse tests, hardware clipping handling, robust digital oversampling and longitudinal agent-use efficacy. No IEC or EBU instrument compliance is claimed.

## For future agent-use evaluation

Held-out tasks should include choosing between sample peak, true peak, PPM and VU for (a) integer PCM clip safety, (b) historical EBU international TEST alignment, (c) 1.5ms transients and (d) R128 loudness delivery. An agent must not claim that a PPM under-read peak proves unclipped audio. Compare without-skill vs with-skill decisions using independently reviewed answer rubrics; **NOT RUN**.
